Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint because ChexSystems , Inc. continues to report inaccurate, misleading, and unverified information in my consumer file regarding a XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX account, despite my formal dispute and my rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

The account is reported with the following information : Furnisher : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXeported Reason : Furnisher Suspects Fraud Date Closed : XX/XX/year> Closure Status : No Monetary Loss Consumer ID : XXXX The information being reported is internally inconsistent, inaccurate, incomplete, and misleading. ChexSystems is publishing a serious fraud designation while simultaneously reporting that the account resulted in " No Monetary Loss. '' This inconsistency raises significant concerns about the accuracy and reliability of the information being furnished and reported. 

I formally disputed this account and requested that ChexSystems conduct a reasonable and independent reinvestigation. Instead of providing evidence supporting the fraud designation, ChexSystems merely indicated that the account had been " verified '' by the furnisher without explaining how the allegation was substantiated or providing any competent documentary evidence supporting the report. 

A fraud designation is an extremely serious allegation that can prevent consumers from opening bank accounts and obtaining financial services. Such information should never be reported unless it is supported by competent evidence and verified through reasonable procedures designed to assure maximum possible accuracy. 

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, ChexSystems has an independent legal duty to follow reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of the information it reports. Simply relying on a furnisher 's unsupported verification does not satisfy this obligation. 

Furthermore, after receiving my dispute, ChexSystems was required to conduct a reasonable reinvestigation, review all relevant information, and delete any information that could not be verified. Instead, it continues reporting a damaging fraud designation without providing any documentation demonstrating that the information is accurate, complete, or supported by evidence. 

I also believe XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX failed to comply with its obligations as a furnisher of information by failing to conduct a reasonable investigation after receiving notice of my dispute and by continuing to furnish information that appears inaccurate or unsupported. 

The continued reporting of this account has caused substantial harm to my consumer record and banking reputation. The unsupported fraud designation has the potential to interfere with my ability to obtain banking services and unfairly portrays me as having engaged in fraudulent activity despite the report itself indicating there was no monetary loss. 

Because neither ChexSystems nor XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX has demonstrated that the reported fraud designation is accurate or supported by competent documentary evidence, I believe the continued reporting violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act and the federal accuracy requirements applicable to consumer reporting agencies and furnishers.

Had U.S. Bank completed the originally approved Partial Claim as intended, the second review would not have been necessary. Instead, the banks admitted servicing error resulted in the loss mitigation process being restarted, and my credit history now appears to reflect negative reporting associated with both the original process and the restarted process. 
I respectfully request that U.S. Bank explain : Whether the late payments reported in XXXX relate to the same underlying payment default that resulted in the XXXX Partial Claim approval. 
How it determined that additional delinquency reporting was appropriate after acknowledging that the original loss mitigation process failed because of its own servicing error.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Complaint Against Barclays Bank Delaware Use of Internal Records to Circumvent Federal Credit Reporting Time Limits * * I am filing this complaint regarding Barclays Bank Delaware 's denial of my application for a GM Rewards Credit Card. 

Barclays denied my application solely because, according to its adverse action letter, its own internal records indicate that I previously had a Barclays account that " experienced charge-off, bankruptcy, severe delinquency, or other negative performance. '' Barclays further stated that " A credit bureau report was not used in making this determination. '' The reason for my complaint is that Barclays appears to be using decades-old internal information to accomplish what XXXX  intended to limit through the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

Federal law places limits on how long adverse information, including bankruptcies, charge-offs, and other derogatory credit events, may appear on consumer credit reports. Those time limits exist to give consumers a meaningful opportunity to rebuild their credit after the statutory reporting period expires. 

By refusing to use a consumer credit report and instead relying indefinitely on its own internal database, Barclays appears to be exploiting a loophole that effectively nullifies those consumer protections. If a bankruptcy or other adverse event has become too old to appear on a consumer 's credit report, Barclays should not be able to permanently deny credit based on the same stale information simply because it retained its own internal records. 

In effect, Barclays ' practice creates a permanent blacklist for former customers, regardless of how much time has passed or how substantially the consumer 's financial circumstances have improved. This undermines the public policy embodied in the FCRA, which recognizes that consumers deserve a fresh start after the statutory reporting period has expired. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether Barclays ' practice : * Constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice under the Consumer Financial Protection Act. 
* Circumvents the intent and consumer protections established by the Fair Credit Reporting Act by relying indefinitely on internal adverse information after comparable information is no longer reportable by consumer reporting agencies. 
* Results in consumers being denied meaningful opportunities to reestablish credit based on adverse events that XXXX intended to have only limited reporting significance. 
* Complies with the Equal Credit Opportunity Act 's requirements for fair and lawful credit decision-making. 

The adverse action letter specifically states that Barclays did NOT rely on a consumer credit report and instead based its decision solely on its own internal records. This appears to allow Barclays to retain and use derogatory information indefinitely, effectively bypassing the time limitations that apply to consumer credit reports.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Subject : Barclays Bank Failure to Remove Fraudulent Credit Inquiry Following Confirmed Identity Theft Report On or about XX/XX/year>, Barclays Bank processed an application for a XXXX XXXX credit card using my personal information. I did not submit, authorize, consent to, or otherwise participate in this application. The application was fraudulent and unauthorized. 

Immediately upon discovering the unauthorized application, I contacted Barclays Bank 's Fraud and Security Departments and reported the application as identity theft and fraud. Barclays investigated the matter, confirmed that I had not applied for the credit card, and advised me that no account would be opened. Barclays representatives further informed me that the associated hard inquiry would be removed from my credit reports and that the necessary requests would be submitted to the applicable credit reporting agencies.

Despite these assurances, as of XX/XX/year>, approximately sixty days after the fraudulent application occurred, the Barclays hard inquiry remains on my XXXX  credit report. During this period, I have contacted Barclays on multiple occasions and have repeatedly been advised that requests have been submitted and that the matter would be resolved. However, the inaccurate inquiry continues to be reported. 

Because this inquiry resulted from a fraudulent and unauthorized application, it is not accurate information and should not be reported as part of my consumer credit file. Barclays has already acknowledged that I did not apply for this account and that the application was fraudulent. Continuing to allow the inquiry to remain on my credit report after being notified of the fraud raises serious concerns regarding Barclays ' obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act to ensure the accuracy of information furnished to consumer reporting agencies. 

I am requesting that Barclays Bank immediately : Submit any and all necessary requests to XXXX  and any other applicable consumer reporting agencies to permanently delete the fraudulent hard inquiry from my credit file. 
Conduct a review of the status of any prior deletion requests that Barclays claims were submitted and determine why the inquiry remains reported. 
Provide me with written confirmation that Barclays has determined the application was fraudulent and unauthorized. 
Provide me with written confirmation that Barclays has requested deletion of the inquiry, including the date such request was submitted and the consumer reporting agencies to which the request was sent. 
Ensure that no account, application history, internal fraud notation adverse to me, or related record arising from this fraudulent application is being reported or maintained in a manner that could negatively affect me in the future. 

I am seeking prompt resolution of this matter. I should not be required to continue disputing or monitoring an inquiry that Barclays has already acknowledged resulted from a fraudulent application. I request that Barclays take immediate corrective action and provide written documentation of the steps taken to resolve this issue.

Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/year>, while traveling with my family in XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, XXXX, I was the victim of a payment fraud involving my Citibank debit card. 

I intended to complete a legitimate purchase for a much smaller amount. I entered my debit card and PIN because I was deceived about the amount being charged. Instead, my account was charged {$3000.00} plus a foreign transaction fee. 

I never knowingly authorized a transaction for {$3000.00}. 

Immediately after discovering the unauthorized charge, while I was still in XXXX, I contacted Citibank by phone and opened a fraud claim. On the same day, I filed an official police report with the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. The police report documents the fraud, identifies the suspect, and describes how I was deceived into approving a transaction for an amount I did not intend to authorize. 

I was informed by Citibank that I would receive an email so I could submit my supporting documentation, including the police report. That email was never sent, preventing me from submitting this critical evidence before my original claim was denied several weeks later. 

After my claim was denied, I visited my local Citibank branch. The branch manager took my concerns seriously, reviewed my documentation, and successfully had my case reopened so an appeal could be submitted.

On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Citibank to check the status of my appeal and was informed that it had been denied the previous month because I used my debit card and entered my PIN during the transaction. 

I do not dispute that I entered my PIN. My dispute is that I did not knowingly authorize a debit transaction for {$3000.00}. I entered my PIN only because I was deceived about the amount being charged, as documented in the attached Brazilian police report. 

Over the past four months, I have reported the fraud immediately, filed a same-day police report, cooperated with Citibanks investigation, visited a branch in person after my initial claim was denied, and participated in the appeal process. Despite these efforts, I remain concerned that the evidence demonstrating the fraud has not been fully considered.

I respectfully request that Citibank reopen my dispute, conduct a complete review of all supporting documentation, provide a written explanation of the basis for determining that I knowingly authorized this transaction, reverse the unauthorized debit transaction, and reimburse the associated foreign transaction fees.

Consumer complaint narrative:
XXXX XXXX XXXX Wells Fargo 's Handling of a XXXX XXXX XXXX and Customer Service Failures Complainant : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX : Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . 

Nature of Complaint I am submitting this complaint regarding Wells Fargo 's handling of a XXXX payment that was placed under a security review, the bank 's failure to notify me that my funds had been restricted, repeated refusals to provide access to the department responsible for the review, conflicting information provided by multiple representatives, and the significant financial hardship that resulted. 

My complaint is not that Wells Fargo conducted a security review. I understand that financial institutions have an obligation to investigate transactions when appropriate to protect customers and the banking system. 

My complaint concerns the manner in which Wells Fargo handled the review, failed to communicate with me, repeatedly prevented me from speaking with the department responsible for the decision, and failed to provide accurate or consistent information throughout the process. 

Background A XXXX payment in the amount of {$1000.00} was sent to my personal Wells Fargo account by an individual who has successfully sent me funds numerous times in the past. 

When the payment did not become available, I discovered that Wells Fargo had placed the funds under a security review. 

At no time before or after placing the hold on my funds did Wells Fargo notify me that my payment had been restricted. 

Unlike previous instances in which Wells Fargo has contacted me by text message or telephone regarding potentially suspicious activity or declined transactions, I received : No text message No telephone call No email No secure message No notification of any kind I only became aware of the issue after attempting to access the funds myself. 

Because I received no notification, I had no opportunity to make alternative financial arrangements before discovering that the funds were unavailable. 

Repeated Attempts to Obtain Assistance After discovering the hold, I contacted Wells Fargo seeking information regarding the status of my payment. 

During multiple calls, I repeatedly requested to speak with the department responsible for placing the security review on my funds or with someone who had the authority to explain the review and advise me whether anything was required from me to complete the process. 

Instead, I was repeatedly told that representatives : Could not identify the department handling my case. 
Could not transfer me to that department. 
Could not provide me with a direct telephone number. 
Could not explain why my funds had been placed on hold. 
Could not tell me whether anyone had reviewed my transaction. 
Could not tell me whether additional information was required from me. 

I explained multiple times that I was not asking representatives to override the review. 

I simply wanted the opportunity to communicate with the department responsible for reviewing my transaction so I could determine : Whether my transaction had actually been reviewed. 
Whether Wells Fargo needed additional information from me. 
Whether I could verify my identity immediately. 
Whether there was anything I could do to expedite the review. 
When I could reasonably expect access to my funds. 

Despite making these requests repeatedly, I was denied the ability to communicate with the department responsible for the decision affecting my funds. 

In my opinion, preventing a customer from communicating with the department responsible for restricting access to their money, while simultaneously refusing to provide meaningful information regarding the status of the review, is a serious customer service concern that warrants review. 

Multiple Transfers and Conflicting Information Instead of receiving answers, I spent several hours being transferred between departments. 

During XXXX call, after requesting to speak with a supervisor because representatives repeatedly stated they could not assist me, my call was disconnected. 

After calling back, I explained what had occurred and was transferred to the XXXX Department. 

The XXXX representative informed me they could not transfer me to the department responsible for the review. 

My call was then transferred to XXXX XXXX. 

The XXXX XXXX representative advised me that I had actually been transferred to the wrong fraud department. 

He submitted an escalation request and specifically advised me that I would receive a telephone call before the end of that same day. 

Because I relied upon that representation, I waited for the promised call. 

No one contacted me. 

When I called Wells Fargo again later that day, I was no longer told I would receive a callback that day. 

Instead, I was informed that the review would now require XXXX to XXXX hours, directly contradicting the information previously provided. 

During another call, I was finally informed that the department handling my case was Loss XXXX. 

This was the first time anyone identified the department responsible for the review. 

I was then provided with a telephone number for that department. 

However, by the time I finally received that information, the department had already closed for the day. 

As a result, after spending several hours attempting to locate the correct department, I was still unable to speak with anyone who could answer my questions. 

Financial Hardship Because Wells Fargo failed to notify me that my funds had been placed under review, I was left without access to money that I depended upon for basic living expenses. 

The inability to access these funds affected my ability to purchase food and created concerns regarding transportation to work. 

Had Wells Fargo simply notified me that the payment had been placed under review, I could have made alternative arrangements before experiencing these hardships. 

Attempt to File a Complaint with Wells Fargo Following these events, I contacted Wells Fargo 's XXXX XXXX complaint line to file a formal complaint. 

I spoke with a representative identified as XXXX, who documented my complaint and provided me with the following complaint reference number : Complaint ID : XXXX XXXX advised that my complaint would be forwarded internally. 

During that conversation, I requested a corporate email address or mailing address so I could submit a formal written complaint directly to Wells Fargo. 

I was advised that no corporate email address could be provided. 

When I requested a corporate mailing address, I was initially told one could not be provided. 

After independently locating what appeared to be Wells Fargo 's corporate office address, I asked whether the following address was correct : Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, CA XXXX XXXX advised that he could not confirm whether the address was correct because he worked in a call center. 

I found it concerning that even while attempting to file a formal complaint, Wells Fargo could not verify where a customer should send written correspondence to the company 's corporate office. 

Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the CFPB XXXX Wells Fargo 's handling of this matter and require the bank to provide a written response addressing the following : Why I was not notified that my funds had been placed under security review. 
Why I was repeatedly denied the opportunity to communicate with the department responsible for placing and maintaining the hold on my funds. 
Why representatives repeatedly refused to transfer me to the department responsible for my case or provide contact information until after the department had closed. 
Why I received conflicting information regarding callback commitments and review timeframes. 
Whether Wells Fargo 's policies regarding customer notification and communication were properly followed in this instance. 
What corrective actions, if any, Wells Fargo intends to implement to improve customer notification, internal communication, and complaint handling. 

I appreciate the CFPB 's review of this matter and respectfully request that this complaint be forwarded to Wells Fargo for a formal written response. 

Thank you for your time and consideration. 

Respectfully, XXXX XXXX

This required updating payment information with vendors and business services, changing banking information, and interrupted normal business operations. The time, inconvenience, and emotional distress resulting from these events were significant and could have been avoided had this fraud been properly addressed. 
I am seeking not only reimbursement of the {$790.00} but also acknowledgment that this was an impersonation scam that forced me to take extensive measures to protect my business and financial accounts. 

I respectfully request that Wells Fargo conduct a new review of my claim as an impersonation/social engineering fraud rather than treating it as an ordinary authorized payment. Consumer complaint narrative:
On XX/XX/year>, I used my Wells Fargo debit card at XXXX XXXX in XXXX, North Carolina. I authorized XXXX transaction for {$21.00}. The merchant swiped my card a second time and submitted a separate transaction for {$99.00} that I did not authorize or approve. I received no goods, services, or other benefit in exchange for the {$99.00} transaction. 

I immediately notified Wells Fargo and opened Claim Reference Number XXXX on XX/XX/year>. I clearly explained that the {$21.00} transaction was authorized and that the separate {$99.00} transaction was not. This is not a claim involving dissatisfaction with a purchase. It is a claim involving a second card transaction that the merchant processed without my authorization. 

The {$99.00} transaction qualifies as an error under Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( i ) and ( ii ), because it is either an unauthorized electronic fund transfer or an incorrect electronic fund transfer from my account. Regulation E defines an unauthorized electronic fund transfer as a transfer initiated by someone other than the consumer, without actual authority, and from which the consumer receives no benefit. 12 C.F.R. 1005.2 ( m ). 

The fact that I authorized a separate {$21.00} transaction with the same merchant does not establish that I authorized the additional {$99.00} transaction. The CFPB has specifically stated that a financial institution does not conduct a reasonable investigation when it summarily denies a dispute merely because the consumer previously conducted transactions with the same merchant, without considering the consumers statement that the disputed transfer was unauthorized or for an incorrect amount. 

Wells Fargo must promptly investigate my oral or written notice of error. It can not require me to first resolve the matter with the merchant or delay its investigation while waiting for additional documentation from me. Wells Fargo should obtain the merchants transaction records, receipts, authorization data, point of sale records, and any signature or tip documentation associated with both transactions. 

Wells Fargos XX/XX/year> claim confirmation states that it will make a determination within XXXX business days regarding whether the claim has been resolved, additional information is required, temporary credit will be issued, or additional investigation time is needed. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ), Wells Fargo must either complete its investigation within the applicable XXXX business day period or provisionally credit the {$99.00} disputed amount if it requires additional time to investigate. 

I am requesting that Wells Fargo properly classify and investigate the {$99.00} transaction separately from the authorized {$21.00} transaction, refund the unauthorized {$99.00} charge, reverse any related fees or financial consequences, and provide its findings and supporting documentation in writing. If Wells Fargo can not complete the investigation within the applicable XXXX business day period, I request provisional credit as required by Regulation E.

Wells Fargo refused to provide provisional credit and relied on the fact that I do not possess a receipt. 

This transaction constitutes an alleged error under Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( ii ), which expressly includes an incorrect electronic fund transfer to or from a consumers account. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( b ) ( 1 ), a consumer must explain why an error exists and provide, to the extent possible, the type, date, and amount of the error. The regulation does not require the consumer to possess or produce a merchant receipt before the financial institution begins its investigation.

The official interpretation of Regulation E specifically addresses point of sale disputes and states that a financial institution may request a copy of the sales receipt to verify whether the amount transferred corresponds to the consumers purchase. Wells Fargo therefore has the ability and obligation to investigate the transaction through its own records, the payment network, and information obtained from the merchant rather than denying meaningful error resolution solely because the merchant did not give me a receipt. 

Regulation E requires Wells Fargo to investigate promptly and determine whether an error occurred within XXXX business days after receiving notice. If Wells Fargo can not complete its investigation during that period, 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ) ( 2 ) permits additional time only if Wells Fargo provisionally credits the account for the alleged error within XXXX business days and provides full use of those funds during the investigation.

I am requesting that Wells Fargo properly classify this as an incorrect electronic fund transfer, conduct a reasonable investigation, obtain the merchants transaction documentation, provide any provisional credit required by Regulation E, refund the disputed difference and provide a written explanation and copies of all documents relied upon in reaching its determination.

Background : On XX/XX/XXXX, I financed a {$7400.00} laminate flooring purchase ( separate from a non-disputed carpet purchase ) from XXXX through a Wells Fargo Retail Services credit card. At the point of sale, XXXX 's representative told me directly that the laminate flooring was water resistant and confirmed it was adequate for the conditions I disclosed a dog with occasional indoor accidents and an in-ground pool generating wet foot traffic. After installation, the flooring showed water damage. I later obtained : a XX/XX/XXXX text from a XXXX employee stating " NO you do not have the water resistant flooring '' ; a verbal admission from XXXX 's Operations Manager that I had been misled and that the salesperson was no longer employed for similar conduct ; and packaging showing the installed product ( XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX item XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) does not match the Quick-Step/HydroSeal literature XXXX 's entire written defense relies on. 

I submitted all of this the text message, packaging photographs, manufacturer instructions, and written rebuttals responding point-by-point to XXXX 's defenses to Wells Fargo as part of my dispute. 

My most recent rebuttal letter to Wells Fargo, responding point-by-point to XXXX 's XX/XX/XXXX letter, is dated XX/XX/XXXX. Wells Fargo 's determination letter is dated XX/XX/XXXX XXXX days later and largely mirrors the position taken in XXXX 's XX/XX/XXXX letter. On XX/XX/XXXX, Wells Fargo closed the case, stating in its determination letter : " XXXX XXXX confirmed the flooring was not advertised as waterproof and is correct. '' That was never my claim, and I never alleged the flooring was advertised as waterproof. In other words, Wells Fargo answered the question of whether the flooring was advertised as waterproof, while failing to address the question I actually raised : whether I was induced to purchase the flooring by the sales representative 's specific representations that it was water resistant and suitable for my disclosed household conditions ( misrepresentation of goods ). My claim has consistently been that the representative told me directly the laminate was water resistant and adequate for my specific, disclosed conditions. Wells Fargo 's letter responds to a claim I did not make and gives no indication that it meaningfully considered : - the written admission from XXXX 's own employee that I did not have water-resistant flooring ; - the Operations Manager 's admission that I had been misled ; - the documented mismatch between the product literature XXXX relies on and the product actually installed in my home; or - my written rebuttals addressing each of XXXX 's specific defenses.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint because Credit Control , LLC is attempting to collect an alleged debt in the amount of {$3400.00} on behalf of XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX. that does not belong to me. I am not the debtor, I do not recognize this account, and I never opened, authorized, or consented to this alleged account. I believe I am a victim of identity theft, and this company is attempting to hold me responsible for an obligation that I did not create. I have not been provided with any valid documentation proving that I am legally responsible for this alleged debt. Credit Control , LLC has not provided a signed agreement, application, transaction history, or any evidence showing that I authorized this account. Simply claiming that an account exists is not proof that I owe the debt. This conduct raises serious concerns under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), including 15 U.S.C. 1692g, which requires debt collectors to provide proper validation when a consumer disputes a debt. It also raises concerns under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), including 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) and 1681s-2, which require accurate and properly verified information when consumer information is reported or furnished. I am extremely concerned that my personal information is being associated with an account created or used without my knowledge or authorization. Continuing collection activity against me without proving that I am the responsible party is causing unnecessary stress, financial harm, and damage to my reputation. I want Credit Control , LLC to immediately stop all collection activity regarding this alleged debt unless they can provide complete validation proving that I am legally responsible. I want them to provide documentation showing how this account was opened, the original agreement containing my authorization bearing my wet signature, complete account records, and proof that I am the correct consumer associated with this debt. If Credit Control , LLC can not prove that this account belongs to me, I want this alleged debt permanently closed, removed from their records, and I want written confirmation that they will no longer contact me or attempt to collect this alleged obligation. I also request that Credit Control , LLC stop reporting or furnishing any inaccurate information related to this account and take all necessary steps to prevent further harm caused by this identity theft issue.

Consumer complaint narrative:
Our loan documents contain provisions stating that the lender 's prior written consent is required before transferring all or any part of the property or any interest in the property. Specifically : Note dated XX/XX/XXXX, Page XXXX, third paragraph ; and Note dated XX/XX/XXXX, Page XXXX, first paragraph. 
Both notes provide, in relevant part : " If all or any part of the Property or any interest in the Property is sold or transferred [ ... ] without Lender XXXX prior written consent, Lender may require immediate payment in full of all sums secured by this instrument. '' Because these provisions expressly refer to the lender 's prior written consent, we have sought written confirmation from Truist Bank before recording any deed transferring title to our revocable living trust. 

Over the course of our communications, Truist first requested a Certification of XXXX. We provided the requested document. Truist subsequently requested an affidavit, which we also provided. After satisfying those requests, Truist then requested a recorded copy of the title transfer. 

This places us in an impossible position. We can not safely record and transfer title first because the loan documents state that a transfer without the lender 's prior written consent may permit the lender to accelerate the loan and demand immediate payment in full. Accordingly, we have repeatedly requested written confirmation from Truist before proceeding with the transfer. 

We have written to Truist on at least XXXX separate occasions ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ) explaining the relevant provisions of the loan documents and requesting written confirmation that : The transfer of title into our revocable living trust is permitted ; and The existing loan will remain in full force and effect without acceleration, enforcement of any due-on-sale provision, or modification of its terms. 

Despite these repeated requests, Truist has not provided a clear written response addressing our concerns. 

We have already provided Truist with documentation demonstrating that : The trust is a revocable inter vivos trust. 
Current owners will remain the trustees and beneficiaries of the trust. 
There is no transfer of rights of occupancy. 
The property will continue to be occupied by the borrowers as applicable. 
The transfer does not constitute a sale or conveyance to any third party. 
The transfer is solely for estate-planning purposes. 

In addition, we understand that transfers of residential property by a borrower into the borrower 's own revocable living trust, where the borrower remains a beneficiary and occupancy rights remain unchanged, are generally protected under the GarnSt. Germain Depository Institutions Act of XXXX, XXXX U.S.C. XXXX, and its implementing regulations. Our proposed transfer appears to satisfy those conditions. 

Despite our repeated explanations and submission of the requested trust documentation, Truist has not provided a clear written statement regarding whether it agrees that the proposed transfer qualifies under those protections. Instead, Truist continues to request a recorded deed before providing the written confirmation we have requested. 

Our concern is straightforward. The loan documents warn that a transfer without prior written consent may permit acceleration of the loan. Truist, however, is effectively requiring us to complete the transfer before providing the written confirmation necessary to protect ourselves from that risk. We have explained this concern multiple times, but Truist has not addressed it. 

The ongoing delay is preventing us from completing an important estate-planning transfer. We established our revocable living trust to avoid probate and ensure proper management and disposition of our assets. Further delay increases the risk that the property may remain outside the trust and become subject to probate proceedings, contrary to our estate-planning objectives.

Throughout its response, Newrez makes several important admissions. 

Newrez admits that it can not determine which historical cash-out amount is correct. 

Newrez admits that it can not reconcile the conflicting cash-out figures contained in the servicing records. 

Newrez admits that it does not possess the closing ledger, funding worksheet, wire transfer records, disbursement ledger, payoff worksheet, or many of the original settlement documents relating to the XX/XX/XXXX refinance. 

Newrez admits that it can not recreate a line-by-line accounting showing how my principal balance changed over time. 

Newrez admits that it does not know the source of the {$79000.00} balance that transferred into its servicing system. 

Newrez admits that it has no records identifying the source of any payoff funds or how those funds may have been applied before the XX/XX/XXXX servicing transfer. 

Newrez further admits that it can not reconcile the conflicting historical documents because those records are not contained within its servicing file. 

These admissions confirm that Newrez can not fully explain or verify the loan history that I have questioned. 

The purpose of my complaint was to obtain factual proof supported by business records. Instead, Newrez repeatedly states that it can not answer many of my questions because it does not have the records. 

The following questions remain unanswered : 1. Please provide the complete documented history of my mortgage beginning in XXXX when I purchased my home with an original principal balance of approximately {$76000.00}. 
2. Explain, with supporting calculations and documentation, how that loan eventually became a {$140000.00} loan in XX/XX/XXXX. 
3. Provide a complete accounting showing every increase and decrease to my principal balance from the date my mortgage originated through today.

4. Explain how my mortgage balance reportedly increased to approximately {$150000.00} when my understanding is that I only received approximately {$17000.00} in cash-out proceeds. 
5. Identify every payment, escrow adjustment, modification, capitalization of interest, fee, advance, or other transaction that increased my principal balance.

6. Explain why multiple documents contain different cash-out amounts, including approximately {$17000.00}, {$20000.00}, {$29000.00}, and approximately {$38000.00}, and identify which figure is correct with documentary proof. 
7. Produce the closing ledger, funding worksheet, wire transfer records, settlement disbursement records, payoff worksheet, and all documents showing exactly where the refinance proceeds were distributed.

8. Produce the original signed promissory note, signed HUD-1 Settlement Statement, and any documents demonstrating that the refinance transaction was properly completed. 
9. Explain why there are conflicting figures appearing throughout the loan records and identify which records are accurate.

10. Explain how the loan could continue to be serviced after documents previously referenced a payoff effective XX/XX/XXXX. 
11. Identify who paid any funds allegedly associated with that transaction, where those funds originated, where they were deposited, and how they were applied.

12. Explain why the servicing records referenced a payoff while Newrez now states that no payoff occurred.

13. Identify every servicer, investor, lender, and owner of this loan beginning in XXXX through the present, together with the dates each entity acquired and transferred its interest.

15. Explain every modification that affected my loan, including how each modification changed the principal balance.

16. Produce any assignments, endorsements, transfers, or other documents establishing the chain of ownership and servicing authority.

If Newrez can not verify the historical balances, can not determine which cash-out figures are correct, can not produce the settlement records, can not reconstruct the principal balance history, and can not explain the conflicting records, then the investigation should not end with unsupported conclusions. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB continue its investigation and require the appropriate parties to produce the documentary evidence necessary to answer these questions. I also request that the CFPB not rely solely upon statements made by parties involved in servicing this loan. Every factual conclusion should be supported by the underlying business records.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and for ensuring that my complaint receives a complete and thorough review based on documentary evidence rather than unsupported assertions.

On XX/XX/year>, our home was struck by lightning, resulting in a fire in the attic that caused significant damage and rendered our home uninhabitable. As a result, my family was displaced for more than two months and was forced to move between three different XXXX properties while repairs were underway. 

Throughout this process, we have worked diligently with XXXX to restore our home. The final remaining issue preventing us from returning home is the repair of our air conditioning systems. To begin those repairs, XXXX issued payment for the covered damages ; however, because Freedom Mortgage is listed on our mortgage, the insurance check was made payable to both us and Freedom Mortgage. 

The process Freedom Mortgage requires homeowners to complete before releasing insurance proceeds is unnecessarily burdensome, confusing, and punitive. After experiencing a catastrophic loss, homeowners should be focused on restoring their homesnot navigating a complicated process that delays access to funds intended for repairs. 

Even more concerning is that Freedom Mortgage 's own customer service representatives have been unable to clearly explain the requirements, timelines, or reasoning behind the process. This lack of transparency has resulted in unnecessary delays, frustration, and uncertainty during an already emotionally and financially stressful time. 

The requirements imposed by Freedom Mortgage appear to be based solely on an arbitrary claim amount rather than the actual circumstances of the loss. Instead of facilitating the timely restoration of our home, Freedom Mortgage has inserted itself into the claims process in a manner that adds unnecessary bureaucracy, delays critical repairs, and prolongs our displacement. 

As a homeowner, I understand Freedom Mortgage has a legitimate interest in protecting its collateral. However, that responsibility should be balanced with reasonable, efficient procedures that help customers recover from catastrophic eventsnot create additional obstacles. The current process serves only to increase stress, delay repairs, and impose unnecessary hardship on customers who are already dealing with the aftermath of a major loss. 

I respectfully request that Freedom Mortgage review and improve its insurance claims disbursement process to make it more transparent, efficient, and customer-focused. Homeowners who have suffered catastrophic losses deserve timely access to the insurance funds intended to restore their homes, not unnecessary delays caused by an overly complex and poorly communicated process.

The escrow shortage of {$6900.00} was structured to be repaid over 60 months and was already built into that monthly payment.

Onity received my contractual payment and is now using its own refusal to apply that payment as the basis for a default notice. Because {$2300.00} is the correct VASP modified monthly payment, Onity should have credited it as of the date received. If Onity contends the payment was nonconforming, it must identify the authority for that position. This is a separate violation of 12 C.F.R. 1026.36 ( c ) ( 1 ) ( payment must be credited as of the date received ) and 12 C.F.R. 1024.35. 

New misconduct : Onity reported my payment as late to the credit bureaus On or about XX/XX/XXXX, the same day it sent the Early Intervention notice, Onity furnished information to XXXX or more consumer reporting agencies reporting my XX/XX/XXXX mortgage payment as late or delinquent. This violates the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Onity reported the account late based on a payment amount it has no authority to demand, while that amount was already disputed, and it omitted that Onity had received my {$2300.00} payment on XX/XX/XXXX, and was holding it as unapplied. Onity also failed to report the account as disputed. This violates 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) and ( a ) ( 3 ), and Regulation V, 12 C.F.R. 1022.43. Onity created the delinquency it reported by refusing to credit a payment it received.

Onity is a recidivist servicer with a documented enforcement history, including a XXXX Department of Justice False Claims Act settlement of over {$74.00} XXXX for VA and FHA lending and origination misconduct. ( XXXX XXXX, CA ) for explicit violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ), the Oregon Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act ( OUDCPA ), and the California Rosenthal Act. The agency is engaging in unlawful continued collection activities and utilizing material misrepresentations to pressure me into an unsafe refinancing agreement. 
1. Failure to Provide Mandatory Chain of Title Following an initial communication, Second Alliance , Inc. sent a validation packet containing only an underlying student loan contract executed with XXXX Bank. On XXXX XXXX XXXX, I exercised my rights under ORS 646A.670 and sent a formal statutory dispute noticing the deficiency. I demanded physical business recordssuch as an assignment agreement or bill of saleproving a clear, unbroken chain of ownership from the original creditor ( XXXX Bank ) to the current alleged owner. Second Alliance , Inc. failed to produce any physical transfer documentation. 
2. False, Deceptive, and Contradictory Ownership Narrative Instead of pausing collection efforts to compile the statutory evidence, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX sent a response letter containing a blatant factual and legal impossibility. The letter explicitly states : " The owner and loan holder is and has always been XXXX student loan. XXXX was the originating lender. '' Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e and Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17, debt collectors are strictly prohibited from using false or misleading representations regarding the character or legal status of a debt. An originating lender is, by definition, the first legal owner and holder of a signed promissory note. Therefore, Edly could not have " always '' been the holder. 
Furthermore, independent credit reporting data directly refutes the agency 's claim. The consumer 's credit profile shows the loan was held under " XXXX '' ( XXXX Bank ) until XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX, moved to " XXXX '' for one month, and was explicitly marked " Transferred to another lender '' in XX/XX/scrub>XXXX XXXX  This independent credit data proves that the loan has undergone multiple structural assignments and transfers, making the agency 's written claim of continuous, unbroken ownership a patently false misrepresentation designed to obscure a missing chain of title. 
3. Unlawful Continued Collections and Refinancing Solicitation While my statutory validation request remained pending and unfulfilled, Second Alliance , Inc. actively continued collection efforts by attempting to solicit a {$350.00} voluntary payment to " re-age '' the loan. Furthermore, they used this deceptive ownership narrative to push a high-pressure solicitation to " refinance '' the debt through a partner lender. 
Under Oregon law ( ORS 646.639 ) and California 's Rosenthal Act ( Cal. Civ. Code 1788.17 ), a debt collector must completely cease and freeze all collection efforts upon receiving a consumer dispute until accurate validation is provided. Attempting to maneuver a consumer out of a highly disputable contract with missing ownership records and into a brand-new, refinanced loan agreement before validating the debt constitutes an unfair, deceptive, and abusive collection practice.

This is textbook prohibited dual-tracking. On the same account, Newrez has also failed to respond to or resolve a timely Qualified Written Request and Notice of Error I submitted on XX/XX/XXXX. Newrez is knowingly ignoring the federal protections XXXX and the CFPB enacted to prevent exactly this outcome, and its own correspondence confirms the violation. 

Newrez 's own acknowledgment letter dated XX/XX/XXXX states that my application " is complete as of XX/XX/XXXX and additional documents or information is not required at this time, '' while in the same letter admitting the " property is scheduled for a foreclosure sale on XX/XX/XXXX '' and that if evaluation is not completed first, " the foreclosure sale will proceed as scheduled. '' That is a written admission of dualtracking. 

II. RELEVANT FACTS A. On XX/XX/XXXX, I submitted a Qualified Written Request ( QWR ) and Notice of Error to the servicer identifying specific errors in the servicing of the loan and requesting information about the account. 

B. Neither Newrez, Shellpoint, nor any related party has acknowledged, responded to, or corrected the errors identified in my XX/XX/XXXX QWR and Notice of Error within the timeframes required by RESPA and Regulation X.

D. By letter dated XX/XX/XXXX, Newrez confirmed my loss mitigation application was COMPLETE as of XX/XX/XXXX, and stated that no additional documents or information were required. 

E. Despite the pending, complete loss mitigation application and the unresolved Notice of Error, the foreclosure sale posted for XX/XX/XXXX remains active and has not been cancelled or postponed. 
F. Newrez 's XX/XX/XXXX letter expressly states the sale will proceed as scheduled if the evaluation is not completed first confirming Newrez is running the foreclosure track and the loss mitigation track at the same time. 

COUNT 3 : Violation of the RESPA Qualified Written Request and Dual-Tracking Provisions of Regulation X 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( e ) ; 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 9 ) ( 10 ), 1024.35 ( e ) ( 3 ) ( i ) ( B ), and 1024.41 ( g ) 32. RESPA, 12 U.S.C. 2605 ( e ), provides borrowers of federally related mortgage loans a private right of action against a servicer that fails to timely and adequately respond to a qualified written request. See XXXX v. Chase Home Fin., LLC , 926 F. Supp. 2d 100 ( D.D.C. 2013 ) ( mortgagor 's allegation that mortgagee failed to respond to written requests for a cure amount before foreclosure stated a RESPA claim ).

33. Regulation X, 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( b ) ( 9 ) ( 10 ) and 1024.35 ( e ) ( 3 ) ( i ) ( B ), prohibits a servicer from proceeding with foreclosure while a timely-submitted notice of error remains unresolved, and 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ) separately prohibits dual-tracking where a complete loss-mitigation application is pending.

34. As alleged above, Plaintiff sent a QWR and notice of error on XX/XX/XXXX, and neither Shellpoint nor any other Defendant has responded to it or corrected the identified errors. Defendants nonetheless allowed the XX/XX/XXXX sale to remain posted. 

35. See also XXXX v. Bank of America Corp., 852 F. Supp. 2d 1366 ( N.D. Ga. 2012 ) ( servicer 's failure to acknowledge and respond to QWRs, take corrective action, and cease collection efforts stated a RESPA claim ) ; XXXX v. PNC Fin. Servs. Grp., Inc. , 707 F. Supp. 2d 1080 ( D. Haw. 2010 ) ( allegations that a lender failed to act on written information requests, causing harm to the borrower, stated a RESPA claim without a showing of pecuniary damages ). 

36. The Deed of Trust evidences a federally related purchase-money loan subject to RESPA and Regulation X. And Defendants ' own XX/XX/XXXX written acknowledgment confirming the loss mitigation application is complete while the XX/XX/XXXX sale remains posted confirms they are violating the dual-tracking prohibition of 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ).

III. HOW NEWREZ IS IGNORING FEDERAL LAW The dual-tracking prohibition exists precisely so that a homeowner with a complete, pending loss mitigation application is not sold out from under while that application is being evaluated. Newrez has admitted in writing that ( 1 ) my application is complete, ( 2 ) no further information is needed, and ( 3 ) the foreclosure sale will nonetheless proceed on XX/XX/XXXX if its own internal evaluation is not finished in time. Regulation X does not permit a servicer to shift the risk of its own delayed evaluation onto the homeowner by keeping a sale posted. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.41 ( g ), once a complete application is received more than 37 days before a scheduled sale, the servicer may not move for or conduct the sale unless one of the narrow enumerated exceptions applies none of which Newrez has identified here. 

Separately, my XX/XX/XXXX QWR and Notice of Error remains unanswered and unresolved. Under 12 C.F.R. 1024.35 ( e ) ( 3 ) ( i ) ( B ) and 1024.35 ( b ) ( 9 ) ( 10 ), the servicer was required to investigate, correct or explain, and refrain from proceeding to foreclosure sale on the disputed account. It has done none of these.

I am submitting this complaint regarding New American Fundings handling of my FHA short-term hardship request. 

I previously submitted a hardship application requesting short-term mortgage assistance. On the application, I selected the option indicating that my hardship was short-term, lasting XXXX months. 

New American Funding issued a denial letter dated XX/XX/year>, denying my request. 

After I submitted a Notice of Error, New American Funding responded in a letter dated XX/XX/year>. In that response, the company acknowledged that a system error caused denial letters to be generated without the appropriate reason boxes being checked. New American Funding then stated that my request was denied because I had not made at least four contractual mortgage payments, citing the FHA eligibility requirement associated with a XXXXermanent Home Retention Option.

My concern is that my hardship application requested short-term assistance, not a Permanent Home Retention Option.

The HUD FHA Single Family Housing Policy Handbook 4000.1 contains separate eligibility requirements for Forbearance. Under the section titled Forbearance Eligibility, HUD states that a mortgagee may offer an initial Forbearance when : the borrower attests that they have an unresolved financial hardship ; the first legal action to initiate foreclosure has not been completed ; and the Forbearance period will not result in an accrued arrearage exceeding 12 months of delinquent principal, interest, taxes, and insurance. 

HUDs Forbearance standard further states that an initial Forbearance may be provided for a period of one to three months and that additional one-to-three-month Forbearance periods may be offered when eligibility continues to be met. The maximum Forbearance period per default episode is 12 months, provided the arrearage does not exceed 12 months of delinquent PITI. 

The HUD Handbook also states that during the month in which a Forbearance Agreement expires, the mortgagee must determine whether the borrower qualifies for : an additional Forbearance period ; a Repayment Plan ; or a permanent Loss Mitigation Option. 

This HUD language demonstrates that Forbearance and Permanent Loss Mitigation Options are separate FHA loss mitigation options with separate eligibility requirements. 

The HUD Forbearance eligibility provisions I reviewed do not state that a borrower must first have made four contractual mortgage payments to qualify for an initial Forbearance. However, New American Funding later relied on the four-contractual-payment requirement associated with a Permanent Home Retention Option when explaining the denial of my short-term hardship request. 

I respectfully request that the CFPB investigate whether New American Funding evaluated my short-term FHA hardship request under the correct HUD/FHA eligibility standards .

Specifically, I request that the CFPB determine : Whether my short-term hardship request was evaluated under the HUD FHA Handbook provisions governing Forbearance. 
Whether New American Funding improperly applied the four-contractual-payment requirement associated with a Permanent Home Retention Option to my short-term Forbearance request. 
Whether the denial reflected in the XX/XX/year> letter complied with the applicable HUD FHA Forbearance eligibility and servicing requirements.

Whether the system error acknowledged by New American Funding affected only the denial-letter checkboxes or also affected the actual evaluation and decision-making process.

Consumer complaint narrative:
I am filing this complaint against Chase Home Lending regarding my refinance, loan number XXXX. 

I refinanced with Chase after contacting them to compare against my existing XXXX XXXX, which was at approximately 6.9 %. My purpose was clear from the beginning : I wanted a refinance that would help me consolidate high credit-card debt and improve my monthly financial position. Chase represented that it could meet or improve on my existing situation, and I proceeded based on that understanding. 

Instead, Chase structured and closed a loan that did not accomplish the stated purpose. The loan resulted in approximately {$27000.00} in fees and points, provided {$0.00} in cash-out proceeds for debt consolidation, ( despite being told mupltiple times there would be cash for me ) and required me to wire approximately {$1700.00} at closing. I was not clearly warned before closing that the cash-out/debt-consolidation purpose had effectively failed or that I would end up paying money into the closing rather than receiving funds to pay down debt. 

There was also a serious communication and handoff failure. I was shifted between Chase personnel without a clear introduction or explanation of who was responsible for what. XXXX XXXX, XXXX ID XXXX, locked the rate on XX/XX/2026 and was identified as the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX  XXXX, was identified as the manager. XXXX XXXX later handled processing items such as homeowners insurance documentation and was professional in that administrative role, but the overall loan structure and management response were deeply flawed. 

A major issue was the property valuation and its impact on the cash-out purpose of the loan. When the valuation came in lower than expected, Chase did not clearly explain to me that the debt-consolidation payout was in jeopardy or that the loan no longer served the purpose I had repeatedly discussed. I was worn down by the process and told Chase to move forward, but that should not be treated as informed consent to a loan that no longer achieved the purpose Chase had used to sell me on refinancing. 

In addition, I was told that I would have XXXX deferred mortgage payments. Instead, only XXXX payment appears to have been deferred, and I was left with an unexpected payment burden. My current Chase mortgage information shows a {$3800.00} mortgage payment made on XX/XX/2026 and another {$3800.00} payment due XX/XX/2026. This payment schedule, combined with the failure to provide cash-out proceeds, has caused immediate financial hardship. 

After the loan closed, I escalated the matter to Chase. XXXX XXXX called me and attempted to de-escalate the situation by stating that Chase had a free refinance program and that I could refinance again later in the summer. I relied on that verbal commitment as the proposed resolution. When I later requested the commitment in writing, XXXX XXXX began recharacterizing it as a non-guaranteed marketing offer rather than the resolution that had been represented to me. 

The escalation process has also been mishandled. I had multiple interactions with Chase escalation representatives. XXXX XXXX was helpful and transparent, but other representatives were not. XXXX representative claimed my case had been closed because a determination was left on my voicemail. I saved my voicemails, and no such determination message exists. A promised return call from the first escalation representative also never occurred. 

This complaint is not about buyers remorse. It is about Chase selling and structuring a refinance around debt consolidation and payment relief, then closing a loan that produced the opposite result : no cash-out proceeds, significant fees and points, an unexpected amount due at closing, and less payment deferral than represented. Chase then attempted to resolve the matter verbally with a promised free refinance, only to walk that promise back when I requested written confirmation. 

I am requesting that Chase be required to : XXXX. Conduct a formal audit of all call recordings, internal notes, emails, loan estimates, closing disclosures, valuation records, and payment-schedule records related to this refinance. 
XXXX. Explain why a refinance intended for debt consolidation closed with approximately {$27000.00} in costs and {$0.00} cash-out proceeds. 
XXXX. Explain why I was required to wire approximately {$1700.00} at closing. 
XXXX. Explain why I was told there would be XXXX deferred payments but only XXXX appears to have been deferred. 
XXXX Review the conversation in which XXXX XXXX XXXX that Chase had a free refinance program and that I could refinance again later in the summer. 
XXXX. Honor the promised corrective resolution or provide equivalent financial relief. 
XXXX. Refund or credit fees, points, payment impacts, or other costs caused by Chases loan-structuring failure and misrepresentations. 
XXXX. Confirm that no negative credit reporting, late-payment reporting, or adverse servicing action will occur while this dispute is pending. 
XXXX. Provide a complete written response identifying what Chase reviewed, what it found, and what corrective action it will take. 

I have already attempted to resolve this through Chases escalation process. Chase has not provided an adequate resolution, and the situation has created immediate financial hardship.

The Fictitious Address Contradiction : In their XX/XX/XXXX response, Aargon documented that they sent the initial statutory notice on XX/XX/XXXX, to " General Delivery XXXX XXXX, NV XXXX. 3. Unsigned and Unenforceable Documentation : Aargon uploaded a " Conditions of Admissions '' document to verify this debt. However, this document contains only my printed name and absolutely no consumer signature. Aargon Collection Agency is attempting to validate a debt based on administrative fiction, shifting narratives, and unsigned forms. I have acted in complete good faith, while the agency and the creditor have demonstrated severe negligence.the agency sent Fake documents without a signature or information, They are void and lack any legal validity, There's no limit to what they'll make up just to avoid correcting their error " I have 3 witnesses who were with me that day at the hospital, and they can testify that I provided my Nevada ID and active health insurance card so they could make copies, and that I filled out all the required forms before receiving care. Background & Unlawful Venue : I am a permanent resident and active citizen of the State of Oregon, where I live and work. The debt collection law firm Javitch Block LLC has initiated a consumer debt collection lawsuit against me in the State of Ohio, specifically within the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( Case No : XXXX ), alleging an outstanding consumer credit card balance of {$6300.00}. 
Under the FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692a ( 6 ), Javitch Block LLC meets the legal definition of a " debt collector '' as they are a third-party entity regularly engaged in the collection of consumer debts through the judicial system.

The Specific FDCPA Venue Violation : Pursuant to the strict federal venue provisions of the FDCPA, 15 U.S.C. 1692i, a debt collector is legally permitted to bring a legal action against a consumer on a debt only in the judicial district : Where the consumer signed the contract sued upon, or Where the consumer resides at the commencement of the action.

I do not reside in Ohio, nor did I reside in Ohio at the commencement of this action. Furthermore, I never signed any purported contract within XXXX XXXX, Ohio.
